answer: Cross-Epoch Behavior Consistency Rule. Each identity must harbor a persistent behavioural fingerprint across epochs. Enforcement compares an identity's action distribution in epoch N against its own history; inconsistent shifts trigger quarantine. A sybil farm must therefore maintain many distinct, internally consistent histories over time, not just pass one snapshot. The cost is continuous divergence management: each clone needs an independent long-run behavioral relic that stays coherent under audit.
